title: Product Loop Register Update
statement: Let $C,e,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{mode}$ and $\mathrm{outer}$ be Boolean values, let $f$ map finite Boolean strings to finite Boolean strings, let $h$ be a finite Boolean string, let $k\in\mathrm{Fin}(e+2)$, and let $v$ be a vector of fourteen natural-number registers. Suppose every register of $v$ is at most $B$, register $6$ is zero, $v(10)\le v(8)$, and $v(7)+(v(8)-v(10))v(11)\le B$. The computation can reach a configuration whose state is the product-clean state with its second flag false, whose register vector is obtained from $v$ by setting register $10$ to $v(8)$ and register $7$ to $v(7)+(v(8)-v(10))v(11)$, and whose result is still absent. Every configuration strictly before this endpoint satisfies the machine precondition and has all registers at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps finite Boolean strings to finite Boolean strings
$v$ is a vector of fourteen natural-number registers
Every register of $v$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $C,e,B\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{mode},\mathrm{outer}$ be Boolean, let $f$ map
finite bit strings to finite bit strings, let $h$ be a bit string, let $k<e+2$, and let
$v$ be a vector of fourteen natural-number registers. Suppose every register is at most
$B$, register $6$ is zero, $v(10)\le v(8)$, and $v(7)+(v(8)-v(10))v(11)\le B$. Then the
specified machine, started in its product-test state with registers $v$ and no answer
yet, reaches its product-clean state with the phase flag false, register $10$ set to
$v(8)$, and register $7$ set to $v(7)+(v(8)-v(10))v(11)$; all other registers are
unchanged, and every earlier configuration satisfies the machine's precondition and
register bound.
